**What I do:** I take the call-out. £400 tonight is rent-money since I emptied the fund [33b996b050d9], and Mrs. Whoever is cold either way. But first I text Mare, thumb actually pressing this time:

> "Emergency call-out. Boiler dead, old lady, no hot water. I'll be late — 7:30, maybe 8. Don't order. I'm coming. Wear the green thing. — E"

Then I ring Mum back and say the hard part *before* Sunday, not after:

> "Mum — we'll be there. But you don't spring Callum on Mare at our table. You tell her yourself, and you tell her tonight."

That's one untold thing killed. Two left. At the restaurant, before the mains, I put the phone face-down and say:

> "Mum's bringing Callum Sunday. To celebrate us sorting things out — her words. I should've told you Tuesday. I'm telling you now."

And then, because Dad never did and I swore at 17:

> "Last night I asked 'then what' and you turned to the wall. I'm asking again. Then what, Mare? Say it ugly if you have to. I'm not leaving the table till I've heard it."

If Beata's Leeds appointment comes up, I say yes before Mare finishes the sentence. I don't know why it matters yet — that's exactly why I say yes.

- **Fear/anxiety — 8/10.** Moved by "her proper talk" sitting in my chest like swallowed stones; I've rehearsed apologies since 4:40.

- **Happiness — 3/10.** Moved up one by writing "wear the green thing."
- **Surprise — 0.** Nothing surprises me today. That's the saddest line here.

Drive-law says I steer toward repair, four seeds out of five [2c42e1f47e8d, 09d3999016fc, 5fcbab072563, 33b996b050d9]. Tonight I drive home late, but I drive home.
